meta.subtitle: Revenue up 24.6% in Q2'26 and the stock at ~6.3x FY27E earnings, but an unexplained late-September fall postdates the last outlook

analystSentiment.commentary:
We rate EverQuote a HOLD with an $18.00–$24.00 target range. At $19.50 the stock trades at ~6.3x consensus FY27E EPS, with $192.3 million of cash and no outstanding debt at June 30, 2026. The second quarter of 2026 showed the marketplace still growing, with revenue up 24.6% year over year to $195.1 million.

Two things keep us from buying. The shares fell sharply in late September 2026 for a reason we could not find, after the last company outlook was issued, so the newest demand evidence is older than the price move (see valuation). And the business depends heavily on one carrier customer (see risks) while David Blundin, through Link Ventures LLLP and affiliated entities, held 57.1% of total voting power as of April 7, 2026 (see governance).

Base holds the current-year multiple and rolls it forward one year; Bear sends the stock back to its 52-week low. The third-quarter report should show whether the September fall was a warning or an overreaction.

executiveSummary.companyOverview:
EverQuote operates an online marketplace for insurance shopping in the United States. It sells consumer inquiries as referrals to insurance carriers, agents and indirect distributors in three formats: clicks, data and calls. Services are free to consumers; revenue comes principally from those referrals, and the company describes itself as focused on the property and casualty (P&C) market.

The business reports as a single segment, with revenue broken out by insurance vertical in the 10-Q. Auto dominates: the 10-K says "a substantial majority of the referrals made through our marketplace are for automotive insurance," and the 10-Q says the company derived 89% of revenue from auto insurance providers in the six months ended June 30, 2026. The auto insurance cycle therefore drives results.

The company was incorporated in 2008, is based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, and changed its name from AdHarmonics, Inc. in November 2014. The proxy statement filed April 23, 2026 states it is a "controlled company" under Nasdaq rules.

thesis.label: HOLD
thesis.body: The operating record is strong and the multiple is low. FY25 revenue of $692.5M (+38.5%) and FY25 free cash flow of $90.3M show what the marketplace earns when carriers are spending, and at ~6.3x FY27E EPS with net cash the shares do not need a rerating to work. What stops us at HOLD is timing: the shares fell sharply in late September 2026 without a captured explanation, and the last company outlook predates that fall, so we cannot tell whether carrier demand has turned. Outside investors hold a minority of the vote, which limits their say in how the company would respond.

catalysts: Third-quarter 2026 results, company data following the late-September share-price fall (see growth for the outlook).
Continued buybacks funded from operating cash flow (see capital allocation).
Launch of the new data and AI products the CEO said would come in the back half of 2026 (see growth).
Progress toward the CFO's stated path to $1 billion in revenue (see growth).
risks: Customer concentration with no minimum spend commitments (see risks).
Carrier spending cuts when auto underwriting deteriorates (see risks).
Voting control and related-party supply arrangements with the controlling holder's affiliates (see governance).
A higher 2026 tax rate that holds GAAP earnings growth back (see income commentary).

income.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.incomeCommentary:
The five-year record is a cycle, not a trend. Revenue growth ran -3.4% in FY22 and -28.8% in FY23, then {+ +73.7% +} in FY24 and {+ +38.5% +} in FY25. Operating margin moved with it, from -18.1% in FY23 to 8.4% in FY25 and 11.0% on a trailing basis. That swing shows high operating leverage in both directions.

The second quarter of 2026 extended the upswing. Revenue reached $195.1 million, income from operations rose {+ 65.8% +} year over year, and operating margin was 12.0%. Adjusted EBITDA, a non-GAAP measure, was $30.1 million, which the press release calls a "record". GAAP net income grew less, to $19.2 million from $14.7 million, because income tax expense rose sharply; the 10-Q expects a higher 2026 tax rate after it released its valuation allowance in the fourth quarter of 2025. Diluted EPS was $0.53 against $0.39. That tax step-up is a one-time reset in reported earnings, not a change in the business, but it means GAAP EPS growth will trail operating growth through 2026.

Gross margin of 97.2% in FY25 overstates economics, because advertising costs sit in sales and marketing rather than cost of revenue. The company tracks Variable Marketing Dollars (revenue less advertising costs) to manage advertising efficiency, and it states "We do not use VMD or VMM as a measure of profitability." Variable Marketing Dollars were $56.9 million in the quarter against $45.5 million a year earlier, so revenue left after advertising grew roughly in step with revenue.

The counter-case is that one strong quarter says little about the next; the operating margin series above shows how quickly the leverage can reverse.

balance.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.balanceCommentary:
The balance sheet carries no solvency risk. EverQuote ended the second quarter of 2026 with $192.3 million in cash and cash equivalents and, per the press release, no outstanding debt; the vendor table shows debt as missing rather than zero, and we rely on the company's statement. Cash is a large share of the ~$687.2M market cap.

Liquidity has improved: the current ratio was 3.33 on a trailing basis against 2.94 at FY25. Total stockholders' equity rose between December 31, 2025 and June 30, 2026 despite buybacks.

The limit of this strength is that cash does not protect revenue. A carrier pullback would not threaten solvency, but the cash pile would not stop an earnings decline either. We treat the cash as downside support for the share price and as buyback capacity, not as a reason to pay a higher multiple on earnings.

cashflow.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.cashflowCommentary:
Free cash flow turned with the cycle. FCF margin was -5.0% in FY22 and -2.3% in FY23, then 12.5% in FY24 and 13.0% in FY25, when free cash flow reached $90.3M. On the current price the trailing FCF yield is 13.8%.

Cash conversion should stay ahead of GAAP earnings for a while. The 10-Q says the company intends to use its net operating loss carryforwards and tax credits to reduce cash tax payments, and the cash-flow statement shows deferred taxes as a non-cash add-back in 2026. Higher reported tax expense therefore overstates the cash cost.

Quarterly cash flow is lumpier than earnings. Second-quarter 2026 operating cash flow fell year over year to $24.3 million from $25.3 million despite higher net income; the cash-flow statement shows a receivables build in the 2026 quarter against a release in the 2025 quarter. Capital spending is small, so operating cash flow passes almost entirely through to free cash flow. One quarter of working-capital swing is not a concern; a run of them alongside rising revenue would be.

multiples.note: Peer multiples pending a peer data source.

valuation.multiplesCommentary:
On every multiple available EverQuote screens cheap: P/E (TTM) of 6.4x, EV/EBITDA (TTM) of 5.9x, P/S of 0.9x, Fwd P/E (NTM) of 7.5x and Fwd P/E (FY27E) of ~6.3x. No peer multiples were captured, so we judge these against the company's own earnings path rather than a peer set.

The two forward multiples sit on different years. The vendor's "NTM" multiple lines up with consensus FY26E EPS of $2.60, so it is in effect a current-year multiple; the FY27E multiple rests on EPS of $3.08. The current-year multiple is higher than the trailing one because FY26E EPS sits below FY25 diluted EPS of $2.63, and trailing earnings include the tax benefit described in the income commentary; trailing net margin of 15.2% above trailing operating margin of 11.0% is consistent with that. The trailing P/E therefore flatters the stock.

The consensus EPS basis is unstated. GAAP diluted EPS for the six months ended June 30, 2026 was $1.04, which looks low against the full-year estimate, so the forward multiples may rest on an adjusted basis or on a heavier second half. We do not call them GAAP multiples. The Street is well above the share price: the consensus target is $29.50 and the lowest target is $28.00, with 6 of 8 analysts at Buy.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: Third-quarter 2026 results show carriers kept spending, the late-September fall proves unrelated to demand, and the market closes the gap to the Street, paying the consensus target of $29.50 within 12 months.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: Growth slows toward the +16% consensus FY26E rate without a carrier pullback. Over a 12-month horizon FY27 becomes the current year; the market holds today's 7.5x current-year multiple and applies it to FY27E EPS of $3.08, for $23.10.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: A large carrier cuts spend, FY27 earnings stall near the FY26E level instead of growing, and the multiple compresses below today's 6.4x trailing P/E. The stock returns to its 52-week low of $13.88 within 12 months; net cash limits the fall beyond that.

valuation.scenarioCommentary:
Base is a time roll, not a rerating on a current-year basis: today's current-year multiple on FY26E is held and moved to FY27E as that becomes the current year. Measured against today's lower multiple on FY27E it is a modest rerating, which we accept because the time roll accounts for it. Base sits well below the Street's lowest target. We hold that discount because the controlling holder and the concentration of revenue in one carrier (see governance and risks) are standing features, not passing ones; this is the one place we argue it.

The weights reflect what we do not know. The shares fell sharply over September 22–23, 2026, and no headline or filing was captured to explain the move. The demand evidence in hand, the August 3, 2026 release and its third-quarter outlook, predates that fall, so it cannot show that demand is still intact. We do not assume a cause. We keep Base at half the weight because nothing captured shows a carrier pulling back, but we move weight from Bull to Bear: Bull gets 20% and Bear 30%, since an unexplained fall of that size is consistent with the market seeing a carrier event before it reaches the filings.

The probability-weighted fair value of $21.61 sits inside our $18.00–$24.00 range and below Base, because Bear carries more weight and sits further from Base than Bull does. Expected upside is 10.8% against a bear-case downside of 28.8%, a reward-to-risk too thin for a BUY. HOLD it is until the third-quarter report fills the gap.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body:
EverQuote reports one segment, with FY25 revenue of $692.5M. Inside it, the 10-Q reports revenue for automotive, home and renters, and other verticals; we do not quote that split here, and the growth section covers how the mix is moving. The company expects revenue from other verticals to be insignificant in 2026 as a result of its focus on the P&C market.

The product is a referral delivered as a click, a data lead or a call, recognized as revenue at delivery. Carriers and agents can evaluate return on their spend directly, which keeps the marketplace transparent but also means spend moves quickly when carrier economics change.

moatFactors.name: Marketplace scale
moatFactors.body: Volume of consumer quote requests and a carrier and agent network give EverQuote something to sell that a new entrant would need time to build. Scale does not lock in revenue, though, because providers can leave or cut spend at any time (see risks).

moatFactors.name: Data and AI traffic engine
moatFactors.body: The 10-Q describes the company as "Fueled by our proprietary data assets and our AI traffic engine." Nothing in the filings quantifies an edge from those assets, and the new AI products are still to be launched. We would count it once revenue left after advertising costs grows faster than revenue across a full cycle.

moatFactors.name: Customer switching costs
moatFactors.body: The 10-K records that one of the "largest carrier customers" stopped paying agent subsidies in 2023 and resumed only certain subsidies in 2024. Buyers can walk away and come back on their own terms.

moatFactors.name: Traffic supply
moatFactors.body: A significant portion of visitors comes from third-party publishers that can change the media inventory they make available at any time. EverQuote does not control much of its own supply of consumers.

businessMoat.durability: We rate the moat NONE. The FY23 revenue decline of 28.8% is the clearest test available: when carriers cut spend, the marketplace had no contractual or structural defense. The rebound since then shows the platform recovers well when carriers return, which is valuable but is a cyclical strength, not a moat. A moat case would need evidence of pricing power through a downturn, which the record does not yet contain.

points: Growth is still strong but the Street expects it to slow. Revenue rose 24.6% year over year in the second quarter of 2026 and 19.4% for the six months ended June 30, 2026, while consensus FY26E revenue of ~$801.2M implies +16% for the full year. A slowdown is already in the estimates, so a second half near the six-month pace would be upside.

The third-quarter outlook, issued August 3, 2026, is revenue of $198.0–$208.0 million and Adjusted EBITDA of $28.0–$31.0 million. Even the low end of the revenue range is above the second quarter's level sequentially. The Adjusted EBITDA range brackets the second quarter's result, so management did not guide to further margin expansion. Revenue near the top of the range with Adjusted EBITDA flat would point to stepped-up investment.

Home and renters grew faster than automotive in the second quarter of 2026, per the press release, and the 10-Q expects 2026 growth from both verticals as carrier partners increase spending. Auto remains most of revenue, so faster home and renters growth widens the base without yet changing the cyclical exposure.

The CFO cited a "previously stated path to $1 billion in revenue" without a date. Consensus FY27E revenue of $882.9M does not reach that level, so the Street is not underwriting the goal on the forecast horizon.

The CEO said new solutions using data, intelligence and AI would arrive in the back half of 2026. No revenue or margin figure is attached, and the 10-Q expects higher research and development spend in 2026, so the cost comes before any evidence of payback.

management.leadership:
Jayme Mendal is Chief Executive Officer and President and Joseph Sanborn is Chief Financial Officer and Chief Administrative Officer, per the proxy statement filed April 23, 2026. Julia Brncic, the former General Counsel and Secretary, resigned on September 12, 2025; the excerpt does not name a successor.

The proxy's Compensation Committee credits management with "effective execution of our strategy" behind 2025's results. The filings point to a second driver: the 10-K describes carrier spend falling in 2022 and 2023 and improving since, so much of the recovery tracks the carrier cycle. We give management credit for keeping costs in check as revenue returned, but its ability to defend margins in a downturn is untested on the record available.

The proxy describes pay as salary, an annual cash bonus tied to financial goals, and equity, with the vast majority of target pay variable. The excerpt carries no pay figures, so we cannot judge award size against results. On balance, management is a neutral factor in the call: competent in an upswing, unproven in a downswing.
management.capitalAllocation:
Capital allocation is buybacks plus internal investment, with no dividend. Share repurchases were $21M in FY25, and in the second quarter of 2026 the company repurchased 578 thousand shares for approximately $9.1 million. Diluted weighted shares fell year over year in the quarter, which suggests repurchases are more than offsetting dilution from stock compensation.

The case for buybacks is the 13.8% FCF yield, and they leave the cash balance growing. Two points cut the other way. Repurchases retire Class A shares while the Class B shares stay outstanding, so each buyback raises the controlling holder's share of the vote. And the 2026 repurchases to June 30 were made before the late-September fall, without disclosure of every price paid, so their value depends on whether that fall was justified.

We still favor repurchases over acquisitions; the 10-Q references litigation settled in 2025 with former owners of entities acquired in 2021, a reminder that past deals have carried costs.
management.governance:
EverQuote is a "controlled company" under Nasdaq rules, per the proxy statement filed April 23, 2026. It uses the exemptions: it has no nominations committee, and director nominees are not selected by a majority of independent directors. Audit committee rules still apply in full. Outside Class A holders vote, but as a minority, so they have little say over who sits on the board.

The governance issue that matters most is related-party spending. Cogo Labs, Inc., a subsidiary of Link Equity Partners, LLC, which is wholly owned by David Blundin, and other affiliates of Link Ventures provide marketing services to EverQuote. The company paid approximately $40.0 million to Link Ventures and its affiliates in 2025, a year in which net income was $99.3M. It states it believes the terms are no less favorable than arm's-length dealings, and the proxy excerpt gives no independent benchmark.

That payment is a substantial sum next to annual profit, and it is set between the company and its controlling holder's affiliates. We do not see evidence of abuse, but outside holders rely on the board's judgment with no independent nominating process to check it.
management.insiderOwnership:
As of April 7, 2026, per the proxy, Link Ventures LLLP held 98.7% of the Class B shares. David Blundin, together with Link Ventures and other affiliated entities (Recognition Capital, LLC and Cogo Fund 2020, LLC) and his direct holding, is shown with 10.0% of the Class A shares and 57.1% of total voting power; the proxy says he "may be deemed" to hold voting and dispositive power over those shares. All current executive officers and directors as a group held 14.9% of the Class A shares and 59.6% of total voting power.

Among executives, Jayme Mendal held 1.6% of Class A; other named executives each held less than 1%. The Vanguard Group was listed at 6.0% of Class A based on a Schedule 13G/A filed November 12, 2024, so that figure is stale; BlackRock, Inc. was listed at the same level, and the excerpt does not show the source date for it.

The holding should be read from the controller's side. Voting power far exceeds the economic stake, and the same holder's affiliates earn supplier income from the company that does not depend on the share price (see governance). Alignment with outside holders is weaker than the headline stake suggests.

idiosyncratic: Customer concentration. The "two largest auto insurance carrier customers" supplied 35% and 11% of revenue in the six months ended June 30, 2026, down year over year from 39% and 12% in the same period of 2025, per the 10-Q. The 10-K says agreements do not require customers to spend any minimum amount, so a cut by the top buyer flows straight to revenue and, through operating leverage, to earnings. The share is easing but still large. The nine-month figure in the next 10-Q is the number to check.

Auto insurance cycle. The 10-K filed February 24, 2026 says carriers cut spend in 2022 and 2023 on deteriorating underwriting performance, a rise in claims, inflation and inadequate policy premiums, and that such cuts could recur rapidly and without warning. The mechanism is carrier profitability: when underwriting turns, marketing budgets go first. Automotive growth running behind total revenue would be the early sign.

Traffic cost and supply. The 10-K warns that a decline in third-party publisher media supply, or a rise in its price, could raise the cost of attracting visitors. Higher traffic costs would squeeze Variable Marketing Dollars before they show in revenue; the third-quarter outlook of $56.0–$59.0 million gives the benchmark.

Related-party dependence. Part of the marketing supply comes from affiliates of the controlling holder, so a change in those terms would move margins without outside holders having a say. The size and terms are discussed under governance.
risks.systemic:
The broad risks run through the economy and regulation rather than through EverQuote alone. The 10-K ties results to adverse conditions in insurance markets and in the general economy; a downturn would hit consumers' shopping activity and carriers' budgets at the same time.

Regulation is a second channel. The press release's forward-looking statements list telemarketing restrictions, data privacy requirements and insurance-industry rules among the factors that could change results. Calls and data referrals depend on consumer contact and data sharing, so tighter rules would hit the product directly.

A third channel is technology: the same release lists risks around the company's investment in AI and competitors' innovation. None of these is quantified in the filings, and new risk-factor language in the next 10-K would be an early sign that any has grown.

body: HOLD, $18.00–$24.00. The business and the multiple argue for owning it; an unexplained share-price fall that postdates the last outlook argues for waiting. The scenario argument is in the valuation section.

We would move to BUY if third-quarter 2026 revenue lands within or above the $198.0–$208.0 million outlook and nothing in the report links the September fall to carrier demand. We would move to SELL if third-quarter revenue falls below $198.0 million, or if the next proxy shows related-party payments to Link Ventures affiliates rising faster than revenue.
